title: Choose the visual world for Gvozdi
question: Choose again: Botanical Folio is now sketched beside Enamelware (the roll), Tear-off Calendar and Nail Grid Specimen.

options.label: Enamelware
options.lineage: Enamel mugs, basins and cobalt house-number plates from Kyiv and Odesa courtyards
options.thesis: Practice as an everyday object you use every morning: sturdy, glossy, rimmed, slightly chipped.
materials: fired enamel with a dark rim
options.viewport: Under the native tab bar: the streak as a cobalt enamel house-number plate (white numeral, inset rim line); below it today's practice on a white enamel sign with a red Begin, then the week as a row of rim marks.
options.risk: Can read as retro kitchen kitsch if decals and chips get sprinkled around instead of staying on the plates.

raised.raise: Every practice carries its sequence number (No. 30), set on today's plate like a house number.
The red decal is reserved for one thing on each screen: today's action.
Week states use form as well as hue: full plate for practised, half-plate for partial, open rim for rest days.
The streak tree is drawn at one fixed scale on one ground, so growth compares day to day.
No chrome besides the plates: no card borders, shadows or gradients; the enamel edge is the container.

options.label: Tear-off Calendar
options.lineage: The wall tear-off calendar (отрывной календарь), one sheet per day
options.thesis: Each day is one sheet: you practise, you tear it, and the stub grows thicker.
options.viewport: Today's sheet fills Home: a huge date numeral (red on rest days), weekday, then '31 minutes on the board' and Begin; the stub of torn sheets above shows the streak.
options.risk: The most obvious reading of a daily habit, and the paper ground sits close to the cream look being replaced.

options.label: Nail Grid Specimen
options.lineage: Wim Crouwel's gridded type specimens, fused with the board's grid of nails
options.thesis: The nail board is a grid of points, so every numeral is built from nail dots on a visible grid.
options.viewport: The streak numeral built from nail dots across the top half, today's practice snapped to whole grid cells below, the grid faintly visible behind everything.
options.case: Strong match with the board (nails are a grid), but the dot numerals cost some legibility at a glance.
options.risk: Dot-built numerals get hard to read small or in Cyrillic text; only the numbers can carry it.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: Days as hairline emission lines on a charcoal band.
options.viewport: A rail of day lines with today doubled.
options.risk: Cold and lab-like for a barefoot morning ritual.
options.case: Loses both axes: no one at the board identifies with a spectrogram.
options.kept: State carried by form, not only hue (week marks).

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Giant lowercase type and flat tiles as the whole interface.
options.viewport: Panorama of tiles with cropped headlines.
options.risk: Reads as a 2012 phone, not a practice.
options.case: Loses both axes: tech nostalgia, a panorama fights the native tabs.
options.kept: Chrome deleted: the plate edge is the only container.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: The 21 days as a purple course over terrain.
options.risk: Too sporty and busy for a calm ritual.
options.case: Loses both axes: racing semantics contradict 'never pressure'.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the active leg (today's action).

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: Botanical folio plates, one plant followed through its stages at a fixed scale
options.thesis: The streak tree as a specimen: every growth stage drawn at one scale, today's stage framed.
options.viewport: A folio strip of five tree stages along one baseline (today framed, future stages dotted), the streak numeral in leaf green, then today's practice on a plate with a green Begin.
options.risk: Cream ground plus italic serif is the incumbent look again; it needs a cooler plate or bolder greens to read as new.
options.case: Adopted on your request: strong on product clarity (the tree is already the progress model), but its cream and engraved serif sit close to the look being replaced.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every session as a numbered catalog entry.
options.viewport: Session pulse plot with a FAC-style number.
options.case: Loses both axes: too cryptic for a glance from the board.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean iOS-native habit app: grouped inset lists, system type, one tint.
canonCard.viewport: Large title 'Today', a ring for today's minutes, streak and next milestone as inset rows, a Begin button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any habit tracker by design.
